disclaimer: This guide identifies documents and offers general orientation only. It does not reproduce or interpret clause-level requirements. Project-specific regulatory compliance must be confirmed by qualified local professionals (architect, structural and electrical engineers, licensed contractors) against the current editions adopted by your local authority.

tiers.name: Statutory or locally applicable
tiers.description: Laws and rules that apply where they are in force. Applicability depends on your location, building type and the authority's adoption.

tiers.name: Model codes and published standards
tiers.description: National model codes and BIS standards. They become binding where a law, bye-law, contract or certification scheme adopts them.

tiers.name: Industry recommendations and ergonomics
tiers.description: Good practice used by designers and contractors. Useful, but not a legal requirement.

tiers.name: Optional cultural preferences
tiers.description: Traditional planning lenses such as Vastu. Personal and cultural choices, never a substitute for safety, structural or statutory requirements.

reviewStatuses.name: Document identified
reviewStatuses.description: Number, title and edition were matched to a source on the review date. The document's clauses have not been reproduced or interpreted here.

reviewStatuses.name: Secondary sources only
reviewStatuses.description: Identified from secondary sources. Confirm against the official BIS or government publication before relying on it.

reviewStatuses.name: Requires professional verification
reviewStatuses.description: Edition, title or applicability could not be confirmed for this release. Check the current version with BIS or a qualified professional.

reviewStatuses.name: Superseded
reviewStatuses.description: Reported as withdrawn or replaced. It may still be referenced by older approvals or local rules.

reviewStatuses.name: General guidance
reviewStatuses.description: Industry practice or cultural preference, not a standard.

documents.title: National Building Construction Standards 2026 (NBCS 2026)
documents.scope: India's national model code for building planning, construction, services and safety. Reported to replace the National Building Code of India 2016 with effect from 30 April 2026.
documents.applicability: Applies through adoption by state and local authorities and by contract. Check which edition your local authority currently refers to; older approvals may still cite NBC 2016.

sources.name: Goa Directorate of Fire & Emergency Services — SP 7:2026 Part F extract

documents.notes: The BIS page reviewed still described the 2016 edition. Replacement details come from secondary sources and a state fire-services document; confirm on the BIS standards portal.

documents.title: National Building Code of India 2016 (NBC 2016)
documents.scope: Twelve parts in two volumes covering development control rules, fire and life safety (Part 4), building materials (Part 5), structural design (Part 6), building services including electrical installations (Part 8) and plumbing (Part 9), among others.
documents.applicability: Reported withdrawn with effect from 30 April 2026 and replaced by SP 7:2026. Many state bye-laws and existing approvals still reference it.

documents.title: Code of practice for electrical wiring installations
documents.scope: Design, selection, erection and inspection of electrical wiring installations in buildings.
documents.applicability: Electrical work should be carried out and certified by a licensed electrical contractor. Amendments issued after 2019 were not verified for this release.
documents.notes: Check BIS for amendments to IS 732:2019 before specifying.

documents.title: Harmonised Guidelines and Standards for Universal Accessibility in India, 2021
documents.authority: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs; prepared by the Central Public Works Department (CPWD)
documents.scope: Universal-accessibility guidance for the built environment across the project cycle, revising CPWD's 2016 barrier-free guidelines.
documents.applicability: Especially relevant to public and commercial buildings and to senior-friendly or accessible homes. Confirm how your state applies it.

sources.name: Ministry of Jal Shakti circular referencing the guidelines (PDF)

documents.title: The Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
documents.scope: Central law on the rights of persons with disabilities, including accessibility of public buildings and services.
documents.applicability: Applies to public buildings and services as set out in the Act and its rules. Private homes are generally a design choice; ask a professional for commercial projects.

documents.title: State and municipal building bye-laws / development control regulations
documents.authority: Your state government and municipal or development authority
documents.scope: Local rules on permissions, structural changes, fire safety, plumbing, balconies and use of space. Interior changes that touch structure, fire exits, wet-area locations or façades may need approval.
documents.applicability: Depends on your city. This app has not verified any city's rules. Society or RWA rules may also apply in apartments.

documents.title: Model Building Bye-Laws, 2016
documents.authority: Town and Country Planning Organisation (TCPO), Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs
documents.scope: A national template for states and cities to update their building bye-laws.
documents.applicability: Only applies where a state or city has adopted it in its own regulations.

guidance.title: Fit kitchen counter height to the main cook
guidance.body: Indian cooking involves a lot of chopping, rolling and stirring. Many designers set counter height from the main user's elbow height rather than a fixed number. Mock it up with a temporary surface before finalising.

guidance.title: Use water-resistant boards around sinks and in humid cities
guidance.body: Below sinks, near dishwashers and in bathrooms, choose boiling-water-proof plywood or boards the maker rates for wet use, and seal every edge and cut-out.

guidance.title: Choose slip-resistant finishes for wet floors
guidance.body: Polished tiles and stone become slippery when wet. In bathrooms, balconies, utility areas and senior-friendly homes, ask your supplier for tiles rated for wet barefoot areas.

guidance.title: Test waterproofing before tiling
guidance.body: Ask your contractor to flood-test bathroom and balcony waterproofing before tiles go down. Fixing leaks after tiling means breaking finished work.

guidance.title: Electrical changes need a licensed electrician
guidance.body: Adding points, changing the distribution board, or wiring a modular kitchen should be designed and certified by a licensed electrical contractor. Ask about earthing, protective devices and circuit loading for your appliances.

guidance.title: Never remove walls, beams or columns without an engineer
guidance.body: Many apartment walls carry loads. Any opening, removal or heavy addition (stone cladding, large aquariums, terrace gardens) needs a structural engineer's review and often society and authority approval.

guidance.title: Keep exhaust and cross-ventilation working
guidance.body: Kitchens and bathrooms need working exhaust. When adding false ceilings, wardrobes or partitions, check you are not blocking windows, vents or AC drainage.

guidance.title: Senior-friendly basics
guidance.body: Good lighting along night-time routes, lever handles, contrasting edges on steps, slip-resistant floors and support near the WC and shower help older family members. For exact grab-bar positions and clearances, consult the accessibility guidelines and a professional.

guidance.title: Do not block escape routes
guidance.body: Grilles, storage and partitions must not block exits, corridors or refuge areas. In commercial projects, fire safety design and approvals are a matter for qualified professionals and the fire authority.

guidance.title: Pooja room placement (Vastu preference)
guidance.body: Many families following Vastu prefer the north-east part of the home for the pooja space. Treat this as a personal planning preference, balanced with light, ventilation and practicality.

guidance.title: Kitchen orientation (Vastu preference)
guidance.body: A common Vastu preference is a kitchen in the south-east with the cook facing east. In apartments this is often not possible; good ventilation, safe gas routing and comfortable working matter more.

guidance.title: Entrance and threshold (Vastu preference)
guidance.body: Vastu traditions value a well-lit, uncluttered entrance and a defined threshold. These are design and cultural choices with no bearing on structural or fire safety.

guidance.title: Sleeping direction (Vastu preference)
guidance.body: Some households prefer sleeping with the head to the south or east. Accommodate it if it matters to you; it is a personal preference, not a health or safety rule.
